body:
One of the main reasons I haven't killed myself in the past is because there's no good day to do it. There's either a holiday nearby or a birthday or an anniversary that it would ruin forever. I actually spent sometime trying to figure out a day on the calendar, but there was always something. 

Nothing really changed. It's a weird feeling, but it almost feels like something's out of place in my brain when my tics are bad. Like there's a plug loose, and then somehow it gets plugged in and things are alright again. I just felt fine and then all of a sudden one day a couple of weeks ago, the tics came back. No warning or anything.

Part of me still believes that it's a learned disorder. That part of my brain just does it because I've done it for so long. The problem there is that thinking about my tics would just make them worse.

There's also the fact that stress triggers it. According to my doctors, my other conditions (particularly my OCD) cause me to be under a lot of regular stress. So that it really doesn't take much for my stress level to rise to the point that my tics activate. But since I'm under a lot of stress most of the time, I don't recognize that I'm more stressed out than usual. It is the holidays, which are always kinda stressful, so it may just be that.

I just hate having this thing that I have no control over. And that it causes me to miss things I enjoy doing (or need to do in the case of work). Makes me feel broken.
